History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed) Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 29-year-old female nurse presenting with a 7-day history of persistent fever, night sweats, myalgia, and malaise after recent travel to rural Vietnam; infectious cause under investigation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Persistent fever for 7 days, hot/sweaty episodes, generalized muscle aches, nausea (reduced oral intake), and significant fatigue.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms started 7 days prior to consult; ongoing.
- Progression: No indication of improvement; persists despite OTC medication.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Ibuprofen and paracetamol (recommended dose) provide slight symptom relief but do not resolve fever.
- Associated symptoms:
   - Night sweats
   - Alternating feeling of being hot and cold, no fixed pattern
   - Nausea (reduced appetite)
   - Mild general headache, longstanding (related to screen use and weather changes)
   - No cough, sore throat, cold symptoms
   - No ear pain
   - No rash
   - No diarrhea
   - No neck stiffness
   - No significant headache beyond usual
   - No joint swelling/tenderness (chronic back pain only)
   - No painful or increased urination
- Systems review:
   - Negative for respiratory, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, neurological, and dermatological symptoms, except as above.
    
Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain (related to prolonged sitting and poor posture; managed with physiotherapy and exercises).
- Migraines/headaches (related to screen use and high-pressure weather).
- Medications:
    - Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented)
    - Occasional ibuprofen and paracetamol (over the counter; dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Allergies:
    - Pollen allergy (hay fever)
  
Social History:
- Occupation: Nurse; currently struggling at work due to fatigue.
- Current employment status: Working; reports difficulty due to symptoms.
- Smoking status: Non-smoker
- Alcohol use: Moderate consumption
- Exercise: Moderate exercise a few times per week
- Travel: Recent travel to Vietnam, returned 4 weeks ago; extensive travel throughout rural areas, trekking and cycling through farmland, exposure to countryside and cities.
- Vaccinations: Up to date, including Hepatitis B

Family History:
- Father died of heart attack at age 68; no other details provided.

Physical Examination:
- No examination findings documented (phone/remote consult; in-clinic examination planned).
- No recorded vital signs.

Investigations:
- No investigations performed at time of consult.
- Blood tests (to be arranged):
    - Thick and thin blood films for malaria
    - Inflammatory markers ("and things like those")
    - Further investigations to be determined after clinical examination

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1: Pyrexia of unknown origin post-travel
  - 7-day persistent fever, night sweats, and myalgia with recent travel to rural Vietnam; malaria and other infections considered.
  - Plan:
     - Arrange in-person clinical examination at clinic.
     - Order blood tests: thick and thin blood films for malaria, inflammatory markers, and other relevant blood work as determined by examining clinician.
     - Advise patient not to return to work until diagnosis is made and condition managed.
     - Document plan for alternative: attend local A&E if unable to access central London clinic.
     - Advise urgent follow-up; administrative support to arrange appointment.

Issue 2: Chronic back pain
  - History of chronic back pain (postural in origin, with physiotherapy and exercises ongoing).
  - Plan: Continue current management with physiotherapy.

General plan items:
- Provide clear instructions for follow-up and clinical review.
- Note to be written for reception regarding required investigations if attending alternative services.

Quality checks (document_quality):

●	Missing but clinically expected elements:
   - Detailed medication reconciliation (including dose, route, frequency for Seroxat and OTC drugs).
   - Full allergy documentation (only pollen allergy noted; drug/food/environmental otherwise denied).
   - No vital signs, physical examination, or lab/radiology results present.
   - No documentation of past surgical history.
   - No explicit documentation of GYN history.
   - No documentation of mental health history despite SSRI use (Seroxat).

●	Internal conflicts:
   - None noted in transcript.

●	Transcript quality:
   - Transcript was clear and detailed; no significant inaudible or missing sections. Some minor missing drug names for malaria prophylaxis (not recalled by patient).
